chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: "When a man divorces his wife while he is absent, he should bear witness to that. When three menstrual periods have passed from that day, her waiting period (iddah) is completed."

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: And this ruling is valid for her only if evidence is established for her that he divorced her on a specific day. If the evidence is not established for the day on which he divorced her, then she should observe the waiting period from the day it reaches her. What indicates this is what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: How is the waiting period (Iddah) calculated for a woman divorced by an absent husband according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the procedural requirements for divorce validity when the husband is absent, emphasizing the necessity of witness testimony to establish the precise date of pronouncement. The ruling distinguishes between cases with confirmed evidence of the divorce day and those without, where the waiting period (iddah) commences upon the wife's receipt of the news, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on evidentiary certainty in personal status law.
